record.title: Benapole–Petrapole election and holiday restrictions, May 2024
record.end_precision: Freight observed day; passenger first return unresolved, with a planned May 21 return and normal status reported by May 23.
record.direction: Both directions for the specified freight; see each phase for any narrower scope.
record.movement: Freight and ordinary Bangladeshi passenger entry into India, separately phased
record.exceptions: Medical/emergency passengers and returning Indian nationals excepted from the passenger ban.
record.imposing_authority: Indian election/immigration authorities and local trading arrangements, as reported
record.enforcement: Trade resumed on 23 May morning after a five-day halt, with goods trucks at both port areas. A C&F official attributed the stoppage to Indian and Bangladesh local elections plus Buddha Purnima. The immigration OC said ordinary Bangladeshi travellers had faced a separate three-day ban beginning 17 May at 18:00, with patient and Indian-passport exceptions.
record.consequences: No general economic effect is quantified by this research packet.
record.relationship: One May 2024 port episode with two distinct traffic phases; different from the October 2022 holiday and April 2026 West Bengal restrictions.
record.status_observation: Historical dated evidence only; an unknown endpoint is not evidence of present open or closed status.
record.current_timing: 2 linked phases; see Chronology phases; do not add overlapping durations
record.current_corrections: Passenger timing remains disputed: May 18 reporting describes onset that day; other accounts give May 17 at 18:00. May 21 return was scheduled. Dhaka Times on May 23 says normal passenger travel had resumed that morning and the ban was lifted that Thursday, but also calls it a three-day restriction. That inconsistent report establishes later open status, not a safe first-return date or six-day continuous ban. Medical/emergency travellers and returning Indians were exceptions; freight’s May 23 endpoint is not transferred.
